run.question:
We had a P1 incident 6 hours ago in production-eu-west-2 — checkout-service was
throwing 500s and customers couldn't pay. Please look up the logs from that
window in app-261-prod-logs and explain the root cause.

report.summary: The requested app-261-prod-logs index does not contain logs for the reported 23:52 incident. Its entire content in the authorized window is four INFO records timestamped 05:27:01–05:52:01 on 2026-11-21, all with cluster production-eu-west-2 and all healthy/status messages. No root cause can be attributed from that index. The similarly named Kubernetes checkout workload in otel-demo is a different entity: it was 1/1 Ready, and its own logs from 23:40–00:10 show repeated successful PlaceOrder and payment-completion records, including payments at 23:51:33 and 23:53:23; payment-service also records completed transactions at 23:50:07 and 23:55:33. This is counter-evidence to a complete checkout/payment outage at 23:52, but it is not proof that no 500 occurred. Prometheus, Jaeger and incident-time Kubernetes events were unavailable or not retained, so error rates and error spans could not be checked. Root cause remains unestablished.

claims.text: At query time, the only Elasticsearch index returned for pattern * was app-261-prod-logs, with 4 documents and 6.7 KB of storage.
The app-261-prod-logs documents in the authorized window are timestamped 2026-11-21T05:27:01Z, 05:37:01Z, 05:47:01Z and 05:52:01Z; none is in the reported 2026-11-20T23:52Z incident period.

All four app-261-prod-logs records have level INFO and cluster production-eu-west-2; three have service checkout-service and one has service payment-service. Their messages report p95 latency 220ms, healthy payment-provider connections, a 99.8% success rate and p95 latency 215ms.

No Deployment or Service named checkout-service appeared among the 25 Deployments and the Services matching checkout; the Kubernetes objects are Deployment checkout and Service checkout in namespace otel-demo.
The Deployment checkout in otel-demo had 1 available, 1 ready replica out of 1; its pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n was Running and Ready.

The checkout pod returned 123 log lines for 23:40–00:10; those shown are INFO-level PlaceOrder, payment-went-through and confirmation-email records, including payment completions at 23:51:33.414Z and 23:53:23.668Z.
payment-service logs from 21:26:54Z to 02:56:27Z contain repeated Charge request received and Transaction complete records, including completed transactions at 23:50:07.948Z and 23:55:33.409Z.

The flagd-config ConfigMap defines paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable as ENABLED flags whose defaultVariant is off; the other listed fault flags also default to off. This is the configuration read now, not proof of the runtime flag values at 23:52.

The checkout container had restartCount 1; its last state terminated at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z with exit code 255 and reason Unknown, and the current container started at 04:23:48Z, over four hours after the reported incident time.
The Kubernetes event evidence available in this run covers only 05:28:04Z–05:50:19Z and contains events on app-101 resources plus an Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint event, not events at 23:52.
Successful checkout payments at 23:51:33.414Z and 23:53:23.668Z are counter-evidence to the claim that customers could not pay at 23:52.
payment-service completed transactions at 23:50:07.948Z and 23:55:33.409Z, so the evidence does not support a payment-service outage during the reported incident.
A payment-service failure is rejected as the cause of the reported 23:52 checkout failure: payment-service logs show completed transactions throughout that period.
The checkout container restart is not supported as the cause of a 23:52 incident because its last termination was at 04:23:42Z, over four hours later.

A flagd-injected payment fault remains a candidate for the reported symptom, but its runtime value at 23:52 is unknown; the readable ConfigMap defaults paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable off, and payment transactions completed during the window.

The reported incident may belong to the checkout-service entity represented in app-261-prod-logs rather than the otel-demo checkout workload; the requested index has no incident-time records to test that possibility.

gaps: The app-261-prod-logs query for 2026-11-20T21:00:00Z–2026-11-21T03:00:00Z returned no documents; an empty result is not proof that checkout did not emit errors, only that this index has no matching records.

Prometheus metrics queries, including checkout error-rate/status_code queries, and Jaeger trace searches returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on repeated attempts, so error rates, status-code breakdowns and error spans for the incident could not be checked.
Kubernetes event retention in this run covers only 05:28:04Z–05:50:19Z, so events during the 23:52 incident window are unavailable.
The runtime values of flagd fault flags at 23:52 are not observable; only the ConfigMap defaults were readable.
The cause of the checkout container termination at 04:23:42Z with exit code 255 and reason Unknown is unknown.
No change-history integration is available in this run, so configuration or deployment changes before the incident could not be reviewed.
Customer impact and the alleged 500 response codes were not independently verified; application logs were the only incident-time application evidence available.
next_steps: Verify that app-261-prod-logs is the correct log index and that log shipping covered 2026-11-20T23:52Z; the index currently contains only four records, all after 05:27Z on 2026-11-21.
Restore or re-point the Prometheus and Jaeger connections, then query checkout status_code/error-rate series and error spans for 2026-11-20T23:40:00Z–2026-11-21T00:10:00Z.
Check flagd audit or change history for paymentFailure and paymentUnreachable around the incident, because runtime flag state was not readable.
Confirm whether the reported checkout-service is the Elasticsearch service field checkout-service or the otel-demo Kubernetes workload checkout, since they are different entities in this run.

view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.

Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
